operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are backtick-quoted in DDL; tables/columns are mixed-case (Ref_Address_Types, Behavior_Incident, Students_in_Detention) — generated SQL must double-quote original spelling.
Tiny DB: every table <= 20 rows; read_schema rowid sampling is a no-op, original_values are complete.
Assessment_Notes, Student_Addresses, Students_in_Detention have NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must be a no-op there, and drop_unique_duplicates has no unique columns to act on.
Assessment_Notes.notes_id is INTEGER NOT NULL but NOT a PK and NOT unique — TS Number fuzzer will produce duplicates; no constraint rejects them.

DATETIME columns store TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (space separator, no T, no timezone); ts_fuzzer dispatch is 'Date|Number(int elements)' — first element '2017-12-05 15:20:04' does NOT parse as int, so Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.
DECIMAL(19,4) monthly_rental stores REAL (e.g. 1297.807, 826.4319) — Number fuzzer with scale=19, precision=4; values are floats not strings.
gender VARCHAR(1) stores '1'/'0' (not 'M'/'F') — String fuzzer will emit random chars, breaking any gender='M' style query.
detention_type_code sample 'BREAK ' has a trailing space — literal-pool values must preserve whitespace; equality joins on it are exact.

Many VARCHAR columns are 100% NULL (line_2, line_3, other_address_details, text_of_notes, incident_summary, detention_summary, other_details in several tables) — TS String sampler drops None elements, so these become random strings, not NULL.
country has distinct=1 ('USA'); state_province_county distinct=16 with 'SouthDakota' (no space) — String fuzzer will not reproduce these distributions.
FKs all resolve to existing parents (parent_exists=true everywhere); no dangling FKs, no self-references, no composite FKs.
Students.address_id and Teachers.address_id are NOT NULL FKs to Addresses (20 rows); Detention.teacher_id is nullable FK to Teachers.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on all DATETIME columns: template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S, range from min/max of 5 sampled originals (e.g. 2017-2018 for Students, 1971-2005 for Assessment_Notes.date_of_notes) — fresh dates stay in that narrow window, so cross-table date comparisons (incident_start < incident_end) often hold by luck but not by construction.

String fuzzer on names/emails/phones: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings of length 0-20 (or up to VARCHAR length), contaminated 50% — emails become garbage, phone formats lost; LIKE '%@example.com%' queries will miss (FN).
String fuzzer on gender VARCHAR(1): random single char, never '0'/'1' — any gender='1' predicate returns empty (FN).

String fuzzer on ref codes (address_type_code, incident_type_code, detention_type_code): random strings, but FK columns draw from parent's generated values, so joins still match; however literal-pool values like 'NOISE' won't appear unless seeded.

Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs: fresh draws in [-10^scale, 10^scale] with scale from type args (INTEGER -> scale 0 -> [-1,1] plus perturbations) — PKs cluster near 0,1,-1,2; joins on student_id still work via FK fill but range predicates (student_id > 10) mostly empty (FN).

Number fuzzer on monthly_rental DECIMAL(19,4): scale=19 -> huge range, but list_max quirk caps at full-range max; values are floats with 4 decimals — AVG/SUM queries get implausible magnitudes (FP on thresholds).

FK fill draws from parent's FINAL filtered column with replacement — Students_in_Detention.student_id may not equal the student_id of the referenced Behavior_Incident row (no composite FK), so cross-FK consistency queries (incident.student_id = detention.student_id) fail (FN).
No PK on Assessment_Notes/Student_Addresses/Students_in_Detention: TS generates duplicate rows freely; COUNT(DISTINCT) vs COUNT() queries diverge (FP).

NOT NULL columns (address_id, teacher_id, date_address_from, incident_type_code, detention_type_code) — TS does not enforce NOT NULL in Python; rows violating it fail at insert and are silently skipped, shrinking tables (writedb.py behaviour).
100%-NULL columns become random strings (String sampler drops None) — IS NULL queries return empty (FN); IS NOT NULL queries return all rows (FP).

Tiny reference tables (2-3 rows) with FK children: TS choose_table_sizes may give refs 1-30 rows and children 1-2500 — cardinality ratios wildly off, so queries relying on 'every incident type used' or 'all 3 detention types' miss (FN).

Date columns in different tables have disjoint original ranges (Students 2017-2018, Assessment_Notes 1971-2005) — TS samples each independently, so cross-table date joins (notes.date_of_notes BETWEEN student.date_first_rental AND date_left_university) almost always empty (FN).
